clue.text: Headgear for a boxing journalist

indicators.note: the words for a are boxing, enclosing, the journalist's letters

parts.note: ed is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A hat suited to a sports reporter covering boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a soft felt hat with a creased crown, a kind of headgear.

clue.text: Female in Slough keeps one wrapped up

indicators.note: the in-plus-slough letters keep the one's letter inside them

parts.note: to slough is to shed, as a snake its skin
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A woman in the Berkshire town of Slough keeps one parcel wrapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wrapped up is concluded or completed, an idiomatic sense of finished.

clue.text: Call a fellow about new advanced drug

parts.note: to bell is to call, as giving someone a bell

indicators.note: the fellow's letters go about the new letter, surrounding it

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a college
A stands for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: Phone a college fellow about a new advanced medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Belladonna is deadly nightshade and the atropine drug extracted from it.

clue.text: 26's mum's parting kisses

indicators.note: the kisses letters part to let the mother's word in between them

parts.note: x is a kiss, so XS is kisses
ma is a word for mum

explanation.surface: Mum blows kisses at parting time.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 down is NOEL, another word for the festive season.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is Christmas in carols, and Xmas is the short written form of Christmas.

clue.text: Topping causing rig to collapse

indicators.note: the words causing rig collapse into a heap and are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A wrecking crane's top part causes the rig to fall down.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing sugar is fine powdered sugar used as a topping on cakes.

clue.text: Crooked mountain at entrance to Trossachs

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for mountain, as in Ben Nevis

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A twisted peak stands at the gateway to the Trossachs, a Scottish highland area.
explanation.definitionFit: Bent means not straight, and also dishonest, both senses of crooked.

clue.text: Signs Cuba's to help Australia? On the contrary

indicators.note: on the contrary turns the whole statement round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: C is the international vehicle code for Cuba
to help is to aid
Oz is a nickname for Australia

explanation.surface: Signs point to Cuba helping Australia, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac is the band of twelve star signs used in astrology.

clue.text: Daredevil spots missing front of Ford Sierra

indicators.note: the spots word is missing a letter, losing it from its start

parts.note: freckles are small skin spots

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: Sierra is S in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A daredevil spots a Ford Sierra car with its front end gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Reckless means heedless of danger, used attributively as in a daredevil stunt.

clue.text: River in spate affecting our outer layer

indicators.note: the river's letter is placed in the middle of the word for a spate, so 'in' marks containment

parts.note: a spate is an outbreak, a sudden rush of cases, as an epidemic is
R is the usual abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A river in flood is somehow affecting the outer layer of our planet or bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Epidermic is the adjective from epidermis, the skin's outermost layer, so it describes something touching our outer layer.

clue.text: Call up the day before receiving approval

indicators.note: the day-before word takes in the approval word, so receiving signals one piece inside another

parts.note: eve is the day before a festival, as Christmas Eve
OK is a sign of approval

explanation.surface: Someone telephones the day before an event, once permission has been granted.
explanation.definitionFit: To call up a memory or feeling is to summon it, the sense of evoke.

clue.text: Colourful singers love parts I introduced

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O

indicators.note: the letter I is brought into the word for parts, so introduced signals insertion

parts.note: parts in a play are roles

explanation.surface: An actor says they love the parts that they themselves brought in.
explanation.definitionFit: Orioles are brightly coloured songbirds, yellow and black, so colourful singers describes them.

clue.text: Quibble can upset the finest

indicators.note: in a down-reading sense upset turns the word for can over, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: a tin is a can
the pick of the bunch is the finest

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that a tin of the best stuff was knocked over.
explanation.definitionFit: To nitpick is to find fault over petty details, which is to quibble.

clue.text: A quiet wood

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A peaceful woodland is pictured.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is a tree and the timber from it, so it is a kind of wood.

clue.text: Red clerics managed to grab second best seats

indicators.note: the rearranged letters grab the second's letter, holding it inside
the clerics' letters are managed, handled and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Communist churchmen got hold of the best seats in the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managed' rearranges RED CLERICS into DRESCIRCLE; 'to grab' puts S within it.
explanation.definitionFit: The dress circle is the first gallery of a theatre, traditionally the best and priciest seats.

clue.text: Needle here when financiers infiltrate Met complex

indicators.note: the financiers infiltrate, getting inside, the rearranged letters
complex means intricate or mixed up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: bankmen are bankers, financiers

explanation.surface: Bankers infiltrate the Metropolitan Police; a needle turns up when they do.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleopatra's Needle is an obelisk on London's Victoria Embankment beside the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victoria Embankment in London is where the obelisk known as Cleopatra's Needle stands.

clue.text: Fortuitous identical moves trapping knight

indicators.note: the rearranged letters trap the knight's letter inside
the word identical moves its letters about into a new order

parts.note: N is knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A chess game where matching moves happen to trap a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Incidental means occurring by chance alongside something else, close to fortuitous.

clue.text: Forest burning? Not quite

indicators.note: the word for burning is not quite complete, losing its final letter

parts.note: ardent means burning, fiery or passionate

explanation.surface: A forest fire is reported, but it is not quite ablaze.
explanation.definitionFit: Arden is the English forest in Warwickshire, setting of Shakespeare's As You Like It.

clue.text: A good place to see art I'd framed in a state

indicators.note: the words I'd frame the gallery name, one letter either side

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: A good gallery is where I had my art framed.
explanation.walkthrough: TATE sits framed between I and D.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a state is the colloquial way of saying worked up, flustered and nervous.

clue.text: Secure report (name redacted)

indicators.note: redacted means edited out, so the name's letter is cut from the word for report

parts.note: a report is a loud noise such as a bang

explanation.surface: A security report has had a name blacked out.
explanation.definitionFit: To bag something is to secure or obtain it, as in bagging a seat.

clue.text: Churchgoers choose to enter civil service

indicators.note: the word for choose goes into the civil service letters, so enter signals insertion

parts.note: to opt is to choose

explanation.surface: People who attend church decide to join the civil service.
explanation.definitionFit: Copts are members of the Coptic Church of Egypt, so they are churchgoers.

clue.text: Illegally sell extra piece of cake

parts.note: to push drugs is to sell them illegally
over means extra, left over

explanation.surface: Someone sells off a spare slice of cake on the black market.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of cake is an idiom for an easy task, as is a pushover.

clue.text: Rude author's penning lines to queen and cardinal

indicators.note: the author's words pen, or enclose, the lines letters

parts.note: the author's is I'm, I am, the setter speaking
l is line, so LL is lines
Anne was a queen of Great Britain
cardinal red is a colour, so cardinal gives red

explanation.surface: An impolite writer composes verse addressed to a queen and a cardinal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-mannered means lacking manners, impolite, which is a synonym of rude.

clue.text: Sound off during shuttle trips

indicators.note: the letters lie within the run of the two clue words, during them

explanation.surface: Someone vents their feelings while travelling on shuttle trips.
explanation.definitionFit: To sound off is to speak loudly and freely, an idiom close to letting rip.

clue.text: Broadcast Beethoven's Sixth in Cornwall?

indicators.note: the sixth letter sits in the Cornwall letters, so in marks containment

parts.note: Cornwall is in the south-west of England, SW

indicators.note: Sixth takes the sixth letter of the composer's name rather than his symphony

explanation.surface: Was Beethoven's Pastoral Symphony aired in Cornwall?
explanation.walkthrough: Beethoven's Sixth is the Pastoral Symphony; here it is just his name's sixth letter, O.
explanation.definitionFit: To sow seed is to broadcast it, scattering it widely by hand.

clue.text: Spook gunners and reserves

indicators.note: the and-word reserves, keeping inside it, the gunners' letters

parts.note: with can mean and, as in fish with chips
RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners

explanation.surface: A spy is listed among the artillery and the reserve troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A wraith is a ghost, and spook is an informal word for a ghost.

clue.text: Two marks for opposing term

parts.note: Mark Antony is one Mark, the Roman general
m is an abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Someone gets two marks for a word meaning the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: The two Marks are Mark Antony and M, the mark currency.
explanation.definitionFit: An antonym is a word of opposite meaning, an opposing term.

clue.text: Coward's book with no verse

indicators.note: the book word comes with no verse letter, which is removed

parts.note: a novel is a book

explanation.surface: A playwright's book contains no poetry at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The playwright Coward's first name was this, Sir Noël Coward.

clue.text: Hire this for day in choppy lagoon?

indicators.note: the day letter goes in the rearranged lagoon, so in marks insertion
choppy water is rough and broken, so the lagoon's letters are tossed about

explanation.surface: A tourist is advised to hire a boat for a day on a rough Venetian lagoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'choppy' turns LAGOON into GONOLA, and D goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondola is the Venetian boat one hires on the lagoon, so 'this' points to it.

clue.text: Shift exceptionally good wine

indicators.note: letters are taken by exception, every other one dropped from the two words

explanation.surface: Someone is moving an outstandingly good wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift is a simple loose dress, and a gown is a dress, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Throw out team during its first half

indicators.note: the team's letters come during the half-word, inside it
only the first half of the team's number is kept

parts.note: its refers to the team, a cricket side of eleven
XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A side is expelled midway through its first half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its' points back to the team: a cricket side is an eleven, so the word cut in half is that number.
explanation.definitionFit: To exile someone is to banish them, to throw them out of their country.

clue.text: Modern US portraitist fires Republican paper supplier

parts.note: new means modern

indicators.note: fires means dismisses, so the Republican letter is sacked from the painter's name

parts.note: John Singer Sargent was an American portrait painter

explanation.surface: A modern American painter dismisses a Republican who supplies paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsagent is a shopkeeper selling newspapers, so a supplier of papers.
